title: Francis Maitland Balfour optics: publication-use closure plus posthumous accretion guard

surviving_group.repository: Whipple Museum of the History of Science
surviving_group.documented_provenance: On loan from the University of Cambridge Department of Zoology; described as having belonged to Francis Maitland Balfour.
surviving_group.historical_box: Wooden box engraved F. M. BALFOUR / MORPHOLOGICAL LABORATORY / 1882

publication_bridge.primary_text: Balfour's published plate explanations repeatedly specify Zeiss objective designations and oculars for embryological sections.
examples: Plate 11: repeated Zeiss C, ocular 1 uses for Pristiurus, Scyllium and Torpedo sections
Plate 11 and later captions: Zeiss A, ocular 1
Plate 21 and other captions: Zeiss B, ocular 2
other plates: Zeiss aa, A, C, DD, E and immersion designations
publication_bridge.result: The surviving A/B/C/aa classes overlap directly with objective classes named in Balfour's publication captions. This closes Balfour's working optical repertoire at designation level, while leaving exact physical-lens identity open where serial numbers are absent from print.
publication_bridge.grade: S for designation-level use; A for assigning one surviving numbered lens to one particular figure

critical_new_correction.object: Carl Zeiss 3 mm homogeneous-immersion apochromat, aperture 1.40, engraved 542
critical_new_correction.chronology_conflict: Balfour died in July 1882, while ZEISS dates its first apochromatic microscope objective to 1886.
critical_new_correction.source: ZEISS official microscopy history / Ernst Abbe chronology
critical_new_correction.result: This apochromat cannot have been used by Balfour. Its presence demonstrates that the current grouped object is composite or has acquired at least one posthumous addition. The accession-level description must not be projected uniformly onto every component.

microtome_bridge.departmental_provenance: University of Cambridge Department of Zoology
microtome_bridge.text_bridge: Whipple identifies this sliding type with the microtome described by Foster and Balfour in Elements of Embryology as the one 'we are most accustomed to'.
microtome_bridge.claim_level: S for apparatus-type familiarity in Balfour's working milieu; exact instrument-to-slide attribution remains open

revised_interpretation: The Balfour case is strongest when treated as a layered production archive rather than a single intact personal instrument set. Publication captions securely document objective classes in use; the Department preserves relevant microtomy apparatus and serial sections; the present optics group also contains at least one demonstrably posthumous component. This makes collection formation itself part of the evidence.
guards: Do not treat the 1882 F.M.B. engravings automatically as acquisition dates; Whipple itself warns they may be commemorative.
Do not attribute the 3 mm apochromat to Balfour; its technology postdates his death.
Do not identify surviving numbered A/C lenses 573, 710 or 1295 as the exact lenses used for specific figures without a serial-number bridge.
Do not claim microtome 6766 cut a specific surviving Balfour series merely because its type was familiar and it came from the same department.
